video_title: Securitize’s $400M Bet to Bring Wall Street Onchain
gist: Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo, fresh off a $400M SPAC listing on the NYSE under ticker SECZ, explains the company's three-line transfer-agent/broker-dealer/fund-administration business model, argues compliant transfer-agent-based tokenization will structurally displace offshore synthetic tokenized stocks, and details the regulatory and market-structure mechanics (NBBO, prop AMMs, chain choice) still gating liquidity growth in real-world-asset tokenization.

insights.claim: Securitize operates three distinct revenue lines under one roof: a transfer-agent business (fee/subscription income tied to assets or volume under management), a broker-dealer (transaction fees on trades), and a fund-administration business (acquired specifically to reconcile 24/7 on-chain issuance and liquidity with underlying funds that don't move 24/7).
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: A diversified recurring-plus-transactional revenue mix (unlike pure-play tokenization platforms) that reduces reliance on any single fee stream as the company scales.

insights.claim: Total on-chain tokenized real-world assets are only about $30-35 billion today versus an addressable market Domingo describes as 'hundreds of trillions of dollars,' meaning the industry remains at a very early stage despite years of hype.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: Tempers RWA-tokenization enthusiasm with a concrete current-size figure, useful for benchmarking growth-rate assumptions in RWA market models.
insights.quote: we're still very far away from tokenizing the world

insights.claim: The primary bottleneck to tokenized-asset growth is demand-side (who actually buys and trades tokenized funds/equities on-chain, currently still mostly the roughly $2.5 trillion crypto-native audience), not supply-side, since asset managers and issuers are eager to tokenize.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: Reframes the RWA growth story: catalysts to watch are traditional-investor on-ramps and frictionless wallet UX, not additional issuer supply.

insights.claim: Securitize completed its SPAC merger with Cantor Equity Partners on July 1, raising $400 million at a $1.25 billion pre-money valuation, and began trading on the NYSE under ticker SECZ on July 2.
insights.speaker: Bankless host
insights.so_what: Establishes Securitize as one of the first pure-play tokenization companies to go public via SPAC, a comparable data point for valuing peers pursuing similar listings.

insights.claim: Domingo frames the $400 million raised as primarily an 'insurance policy' against running out of cash for many years rather than capital needed to run the company day-to-day, with deployment focused on bolt-on capabilities and international expansion rather than acquiring a #2, #3, or #4 competitor.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: Signals capital will go toward organic capability expansion and geographic diversification (from a US-centric base) rather than industry consolidation via M&A.
insights.quote: having $400 million is actually an insurance policy from a company perspective

insights.claim: At its SPAC listing, Securitize let existing shareholders opt to tokenize their shares via its transfer-agent partnership with Continental, with roughly 200,000+ shares opting in, making SECZ (per Domingo) the largest native tokenized equity, ahead of Figure's roughly $200-250 million tokenized equity.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: A concrete, checkable claim about which company currently holds the largest natively tokenized equity, useful for tracking competitive share in the emerging tokenized-equity space.

insights.claim: Domingo distinguishes Securitize's model - a real, 1:1 security issued through a registered transfer agent, on the company's cap table, with full dividend/voting rights - from offshore synthetic 'tokenized stock' derivatives (in the style of Robinhood's or Ondo's products), which carry counterparty risk, fragment liquidity across multiple non-fungible token versions of the same underlying stock, and can strip shareholder rights.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: Gives investors a concrete due-diligence checklist (cap-table status, counterparty risk, fungibility) for distinguishing genuine tokenized securities from synthetic look-alikes.
insights.quote: tokenization was meant to reduce intermediaries not to increase the number of intermediaries

insights.claim: Domingo cites a real failure case where an Ondo tokenized stock underwent a stock split off-chain that was not reflected on-chain, causing the token to trade at roughly five times the price of the properly-split underlying share.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: A concrete, documented operational failure mode of synthetic tokenized-stock products, useful evidence for risk assessments of non-native tokenization platforms.

insights.claim: Domingo says Bullish CEO Tom Farley has publicly described being able to legally buy synthetic tokenized-stock derivatives ahead of an earnings announcement while holding material non-public information, something illegal to do with the underlying registered security but currently uncontrolled in the offshore derivative wrapper.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: Flags a specific insider-trading/regulatory-arbitrage risk embedded in offshore synthetic tokenized-equity products that compliance teams and regulators should watch.

insights.claim: Domingo predicts compliant, transfer-agent-based tokenization will structurally displace offshore synthetic tokenization over time, both because centralized exchanges are increasingly forced into KYC/AML regimes and because a friendlier SEC posture could reverse in about two years, reintroducing legal risk for non-compliant issuers.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: A dated regulatory-risk call (roughly a 2-year window) for anyone holding or building on offshore synthetic tokenized-equity products.

insights.claim: To legally trade tokenized equities on-chain, Securitize must still comply with Reg NMS 'best price' (NBBO) rules sourced off-chain from Securities Information Processors and fed on-chain, effectively recreating a costly, Chainlink-like price oracle for equities that adds real complexity and expense to on-chain trading.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: Explains a specific, underappreciated cost/complexity driver in compliant on-chain equity trading that competitors and regulators will need to solve for the model to scale cheaply.

insights.claim: Domingo says the SEC under its current chair is moving to eliminate Reg NMS Rules 610 and 611 (the price-protection/best-execution rules), which he expects would reduce the cost and complexity of on-chain equity trading, but not for 'a year or longer.'
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: A specific, trackable regulatory catalyst (Rule 610/611 repeal) that would materially lower costs for on-chain tokenized-equity trading if it happens.

insights.claim: Securitize chose Avalanche (for its deterministic settlement, important for reporting trades to the SEC without needing to unwind failed settlements) and Solana (via a proprietary AMM built by market maker 'Jam' that provides continuous, tight-spread pricing) as its two chains for SECZ trading, and is actively seeking a similar prop-AMM/RFQ market-making solution to bring to Ethereum.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: An explicit, sourceable request-for-startup: any team building a proprietary AMM/RFQ market-making stack for Ethereum has a stated potential partner in Securitize.

insights.claim: Fund tokenization is roughly two to three years ahead of equity tokenization in institutional adoption because top-tier asset managers (BlackRock, Apollo, BNY, Franklin Templeton, WisdomTree) already participate, making tokenized funds a much easier conversation than persuading individual public companies to tokenize their own stock.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: Signals fund tokenization as the nearer-term, lower-friction growth vector versus equity tokenization for the RWA industry over the next few years.

insights.claim: Domingo identifies the nearest-term addressable market for equity tokenization as crypto-native companies (wanting their own equity natively tokenized and controlled) and 'retail-centric' public companies with large existing retail shareholder bases - not blue-chip conservative names like Apple or Nvidia, which he expects will not be first movers.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete screening criterion (crypto-native or retail-heavy cap tables) for identifying which public companies are most likely to tokenize their equity next.

themes.theme: Perps, Spot Markets & Basis Trade Convergence

insights.claim: Domingo argues tokenized-equity perpetual futures need a continuous 24/7 tokenized spot market to set funding rates correctly, citing a perp platform that told him it cannot update funding rates over weekends because there is no spot price to reference - meaning real (non-derivative) spot tokenization and perps are complementary rather than competing products.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: Clarifies that perp-market efficiency for tokenized equities is directly gated by the availability of genuine 24/7 spot tokenization, a dependency investors in either product should track together.

insights.claim: Domingo cites a trader's observation of a roughly 100-basis-point spread available between tokenized SpaceX spot and perpetual markets - early evidence of a crypto-style spot/perp basis trade emerging in tokenized equities as liquidity improves, which the host frames as the clearest path to real liquidity growth for tokenized stocks.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: Identifies a specific, quantifiable arbitrage opportunity (100bps SpaceX basis) that would attract professional liquidity into tokenized-equity markets as they mature.

insights.claim: Domingo's rough goal is for the tokenized RWA industry to reach roughly $1 trillion within about three years; even a reduced (from today's outsized) 10% market share of that total would give Securitize about $100 billion in AUM plus transaction volume, roughly 20 times its current platform size.
insights.speaker: Carlos Domingo, CEO Securitize
insights.so_what: Provides a specific, dated benchmark ($1T industry size in ~3 years, ~$100B for Securitize at 10% share) against which to measure the RWA sector's actual growth trajectory.
